edges.description: Defective Sec-tRNA formation blocks the route to selenoprotein generation.
Loss of selenoprotein generation preferentially manifests as early-onset brain and cerebellar developmental-neurodegenerative disease.

nodes.description: SEPSECS deficiency causes early brain involvement with progressive cerebellar and cerebral pathology, producing developmental delay, microcephaly, hypotonia, spasticity, and progressive atrophy.

evidence.reference_title: Case Report: A Relatively Mild Phenotype Produced by Novel Mutations in the SEPSECS Gene
evidence.snippet: Mutations in the human O-phosphoseryl-tRNA:selenocysteinyl-tRNA synthase gene (SEPSECS) are associated with progressive cerebello-cerebral atrophy (PCCA), also known as pontocerebellar hypoplasia type 2D (PCH2D).

nodes.description: SEPSECS catalyzes the final tRNA-dependent step that converts Sep-tRNA(Sec) to Sec-tRNA(Sec). Pathogenic variants therefore impair Sec-tRNA formation before selenocysteine can be inserted into nascent proteins.

evidence.reference_title: The human SepSecS-tRNASec complex reveals the mechanism of selenocysteine formation.
evidence.snippet: O-Phosphoseryl-tRNA:selenocysteinyl-tRNA synthase (SepSecS) catalyzes the final step of selenocysteine formation by a poorly understood tRNA-dependent mechanism.

evidence.reference_title: Milder progressive cerebellar atrophy caused by biallelic SEPSECS mutations.
evidence.snippet: We identified two new families with progressive cerebellar atrophy, and by whole exome sequencing detected biallelic SEPSECS mutations: c.356A>G (p.Asn119Ser) and c.77delG (p.Arg26Profs*42) in family 1, and c.356A>G (p.Asn119Ser) and c.467G>A (p.Arg156Gln) in family 2.

nodes.description: Failed Sec-tRNA formation prevents production of selenoproteins that depend on cotranslational selenocysteine insertion.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations disrupting selenocysteine formation cause progressive cerebello-cerebral atrophy.
evidence.snippet: Both founder mutations, common in these two populations, disrupt the sole route to the biosynthesis of the 21st amino acid, Sec, and thus to the generation of selenoproteins in humans.
